Resolves #20493

Demo B's popup viewport now declares the example palette and Demo A/B stylesheets. A popup intentionally creates no workspace, so it previously never requested those sheets: the same traveling Workbench pane rendered as plain 16px text after loading. Both viewport modes now receive the existing skin through the normal per-window theme loader. The example's viewport/workspace selectors explicitly specialize their Engine classes, preserving their background when the base sheets load later.

Evidence: headed browser reproduction and red/green regression, plus visual verification → native popup appearance required. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1: declared popup styling | `Viewport.additionalThemeFiles` loads Palette, DemoAWorkspace and DemoBWorkspace; no copied or test-injected CSS in the fixed run. |
| AC-2: visual parity | The native popup retains the parent's flex card, background, 34px counter and palette color; the popout host has its intended 10px padding. Headed screenshot inspected. |
| AC-3: regression and continuity | `DemoBKeyboardDetachNL` now compares computed styles and checks the same pane ID, changed window and nondecreasing counter, while retaining the focus assertion. The new assertion failed on the old viewport (`block` instead of `flex`); all three journeys pass with the fix. |

## Deltas from ticket

Loading the skin at viewport construction exposed a cascade dependency: the equal-specificity Engine viewport/container rules loaded later and replaced the main window's example background. The shared skin now qualifies its two selectors with the existing Engine class. No additional workspace instance, pane recreation, theme-loader change or keyboard behavior change. The separate keyboard decomposition is #20492 / #20494.

## Test Evidence

The original headed probe reached mount and network idle with zero CSS request failures. The parent had 43 stylesheets; the popup had 14 basic Neo stylesheets, missing the four example CSS files (the palette contributes dark/light files). Injecting only those missing files in a diagnostic control immediately restored the card. This control established the cause and is not the fixed acceptance run.

The final focused run passed 8/8 unchanged checks: both themes for both examples, the palette mutation control, and all three keyboard journeys. The new popup display assertion fails on the old viewport after 14 observations, so interaction success can no longer hide the missing skin. A fresh no-injection headed capture verifies the main viewport, main workspace and popup viewport ground as `rgb(11, 14, 19)`, and the popup card as `rgb(20, 26, 35)`, with zero page/CSS errors. The shared workspace selector covers both existing base classes (`neo-container` and `neo-dock-workspace`); a container-only attempt failed Demo A's unchanged theme tests and was corrected before this handoff.

Change class: restoration. `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; shared baseline checks run in CI.
